summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that few prizefighters saved their earnings, noting that Tom Allen had nothing to show for his ring career but a saloon on Market Street that kept him comfortably.

metadata.notes: Masthead: Thursday, St. Louis Post-Dispatch, February 1, 1894, page 4.

facts.fact: By 1894 Allen had nothing to show for his ring career but a saloon on Market Street, St. Louis, whose profits let him live comfortably
Mike McCoole, Allen's old rival in St. Louis in the early 1870s, died in a New Orleans home for paupers
The paper said Jem Mace defeated Allen for the world's championship
